partitionClasses.title: Bootloader
partitionClasses.purpose: U-Boot or equivalent first/second-stage bootloader. MUST be signature-verified as part of the secure boot chain (see PCH-015).
partitionClasses.otaTreatment: Platform-required. Bolt A/B (Section 3.7) form their own fallback pair, but the bootloader itself is not directly rewritten by the RDK-B OTA mechanism.

partitionClasses.title: Kernel (A) / (B)
partitionClasses.purpose: Active and standby kernel images for A/B OTA fallback. MUST be signature-verified as a signed firmware image (see PCH-016).
partitionClasses.otaTreatment: Duplicated per slot; directly updated by OTA.

partitionClasses.title: Rootfs (A) / (B)
partitionClasses.purpose: Active and standby root filesystem (ext4/squashfs/EROFS on eMMC, or UBI/UBIFS on SPI-NAND) containing Core RDK‑B components. MUST be signature-verified as a signed firmware image (see PCH-016).
partitionClasses.otaTreatment: Duplicated per slot; directly updated by OTA.

partitionClasses.title: Persistent/Config
partitionClasses.purpose: PSM/TR‑181 persistent data store for customer-resettable configuration (Wi‑Fi SSID/password, LAN settings). Cleared by factory reset; distinct from Calibration/Factory Data (FLC-005), which is never cleared by factory reset.
partitionClasses.otaTreatment: Platform-required; preserved across update (not directly overwritten by OTA).

partitionClasses.title: Calibration/Factory Data
partitionClasses.purpose: Radio calibration data, serial number; written at manufacturing. Non-resettable — NOT cleared by factory reset (see FLC-004 and STG-007). MAC address storage here is OEM/SoC-implementation-dependent — some implementations derive MAC from the stored serial number at boot rather than storing it separately (see Section 3.7.1).
partitionClasses.otaTreatment: Platform-required; preserved across update and factory reset; never modified by OTA.

storageTechnologies.whatItIs: NAND flash with an integrated controller presenting a standard block-device interface (like a small SSD).
storageTechnologies.managedBy: Onboard controller handles wear-leveling/bad-block internally — OS sees a normal block device.

storageTechnologies.whatItIs: Successor to eMMC — same managed-NAND/block-interface model, higher throughput via a different physical/electrical interface.
storageTechnologies.managedBy: Same as eMMC — onboard controller, block-device interface.

storageTechnologies.whatItIs: Raw NAND accessed over a simple SPI bus, with no onboard wear-leveling controller.
storageTechnologies.managedBy: Wear-leveling and bad-block management handled by software (Linux MTD + UBI layer).

storageTechnologies.whatItIs: A distinct flash memory architecture from NAND — slower, byte-addressable, small capacity, capable of execute-in-place (XIP).
storageTechnologies.managedBy: Usually no filesystem; used for raw boot code that must run before the full flash subsystem initializes.

filesystemMapping.why: Block device — standard Linux filesystems apply directly.
Requires an MTD/NAND target; UBI provides the wear-leveling/bad-block layer software-side. MUST NOT be paired with eMMC or UFS — both already have onboard wear-leveling.

layout.note: Partition-level layout (actual measured sizes and usage per partition) is tracked in the spec's Section 3.7 and companion flash-layout.json files, and will be added to this page next. The definitions above apply regardless of the specific measured layout.
